key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr delivered the lowest measured wear rate and best corrosion resistance, while HVOF produced the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: HVAF is a promising coating route for 304 stainless steel components requiring combined wear and corrosion protection.
method: Deposit WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF and HVAF.
Compare microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction and volumetric wear rates.
Evaluate corrosion behavior and identify coating wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF reduced wear rate from the substrate's (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ to (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), approximately 33-fold, and achieved the lowest corrosion current density at 1.75±0.02 μA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion electrolyte, limiting direct extrapolation to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
